review_type: Independent source-informed review of root’s observations and prose; the reviewer could see both the proposed claims and source pages.
scope: Review of the saved South Indian source packet. No further research, new acquisition, field observation or quantity fit was performed.

checks.subject: 408 excavation fields
checks.review_observation: Table serial 2 gives AGM-2, locus 0’-I’, depth 1.40 under Depth (Metre), stratum 2 and rouletted ware.

checks.subject: 408 reading and attribution
checks.review_observation: Prose introduces 408 as probable. The table prints 8/100/4=408; the packet attributes this reading to the report.

checks.subject: 408 drawing identity
checks.review_observation: Drawing 2 depicts three incised graphics on a rim sherd and shares serial 2 with the table. No measured contents or capacity are given in these records.

checks.subject: Tondur physical groups
checks.review_observation: The text reports three rock beds in Panchanampadi cave. Seven and two are the counts of other caves on the hill.

checks.subject: Tondur numeral and referent
checks.review_observation: The author describes three horizontal parallel strokes and the term atitanam for the beds made by Moci. The packet retains these as the author’s published reading and count.

checks.subject: Tondur discovery and date
checks.review_observation: The text reports discovery in 1991 by M. Chandramurthy and places the inscription in Late Tamil-Brahmi, about the third–fourth centuries CE on palaeographic grounds. Plate 8 is captioned c. 3rd century AD.

checks.subject: Tondur plate scope
checks.review_observation: Plate 7 depicts the relief. Plate 8 is a dark ink impression; its available reproduction cannot sustain a fresh stroke count or an independent physical bed census.

checks.subject: Alagankulam_044 exact object join
checks.review_observation: Table serial 950 and Appendix Plate 80 carry the same registration Alagankulam_044. The record gives I-II, depth 380, rouletted ware and reading .. [ . ] ma paṉ #. The labelled photograph shows letters and a separate complex graphic at the right.

checks.subject: Modern depth unit
checks.review_observation: The modern table header says Depth and gives no unit. The packet leaves the raw depths unconverted.

checks.subject: Alagankulam_004 visible stroke scope
checks.review_observation: Serial 910 and Plate 77 identify Alagankulam_004. Four long strokes are visible on the broken photographed sherd. Table Graffiti? and plate undeciphered are retained; original completion and counted quantity are unresolved.

checks.subject: Serial 1 candidate concordance
checks.review_observation: Old serial 1 and Alagankulam_048 share locus 0’-II’ and rouletted ware. Depths 4.10 m and raw 410, with differing readings, support a recoverable candidate. The packet leaves the identity and modern depth unit unresolved.

checks.subject: Serial 4 candidate concordance
checks.review_observation: Old serial 4 and Alagankulam_010 share locus II’-III’, ware, ka reading and a cross-shaped graphic. Old depth is 1.45 m, modern raw depth 145. The packet requests an explicit register concordance.

checks.subject: Four-face object context and hypothesis
checks.review_observation: The report gives AGM-3/A1, depth 0.45 m, a four-sided rouletted-ware rim object, three marked sides and one plain. Values 1, 2 and 3 depend on its proposed die classification. Plate 15 photographs two sides, with a single groove and a branching graphic.

checks.subject: Corrected serial 1 transcription
checks.review_observation: The printed old reading is Pidiyuraiyu. The final observation now gives that spelling, replacing the earlier faulty text-extraction reading Pidiyuaiya.

checks.subject: Chapter pagination including references
checks.review_observation: The title and author occur on printed 116. The Select Reading List continues from 134 to 135 and ends there. REPORT now gives 116–135.

checks.subject: Source and rendering preservation
checks.review_observation: The three original PDF hashes were calculated independently. Eleven saved page renders match freshly rasterized original PDF pixels exactly at the recorded scale; the two pagination endpoints were rendered directly in memory.

limits_of_checked_evidence: Tondur’s bed count and inscription reading are the original author’s published observations; the source image quality leaves independent counting unresolved.
The modern depth unit and the two cross-edition registrations remain unresolved.
The packet does not assign an Indus meaning or fit a joint quantity model.
